To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rats can be trained to display avoidance of saccharin after it is associated with intraduodenally administered LiCl or lactose but not with saline.
conditioned avoidance is a distinct process from conditioned aversion and is not always accompanied with changes in other common indices of appetitive or consummatory behavior.

1) Rats avoid drinking saccharin that is paired with lactose, 2) Rats avoid and display aversion to saccharin paired with a higher dose of LiCl, 3) The higher dose of LiCL also leads to reduced saccharin consumption and a reduction in saccharin breakpoint, and 4) Rats avoid saccharin paired to a lower dose of LiCl without showing signs of aversion to the taste.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of visceral signals in the control of taste-guided behavior, and the factors that determine the nature of these responses.
how visceral signals influence ingestive behavior.
the effects of gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances on ingestive behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditioned taste aversion and conditioned taste avoidance are separate processes.
the conditioned taste aversion and avoidance are two separate processes, and they are not necessarily correlated.
conditioned taste aversion (CTA) is a specific phenomenon, which is distinct from avoidance, but which is not the only form of conditioned avoidance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

conditioned avoidance is the primary outcome of gastrointestinal illness, whereas aversion is a secondary consequence of the more severe effects of LiCl toxicosis. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the conditioned taste aversion (CTA) and avoidance are separate processes that are dissociable in rats.
conditioned taste aversion and conditioned taste avoidance are separate processes that can be dissociated in rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that

conditioned avoidance is a robust phenomenon that can occur in the absence of taste reactivity changes indicative of aversion, and that the two processes can be reliably dissociated. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the separate processes hypothesis remains a valid framework for interpreting the behavioral effects of visceral conditioning.
conditioned avoidance is a distinct behavioral phenomenon that is independent of taste aversion. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved).
